_meta.source: Vox Mana mono identity layer pilot
notes: Color entries define foundational identity language.
Expression entries define routing and blend metadata.
White and Black are active mono expressions in this phase.

W.name: White
W.philosophy: White builds safety through structure, shared duty, and enforceable fairness.

lore.summary: White believes peace must be built and defended through systems people can trust.
lore.narrative: White does not trust chaos to become kindness on its own. It makes shelter, standards, and promises that can outlast mood.

U.name: Blue
U.philosophy: Blue seeks improvement through knowledge, patience, and deliberate refinement.

lore.summary: Blue believes the world can be improved if it is understood deeply enough.
lore.narrative: Blue prefers the patient hand and the well-timed answer. It trusts preparation more than force.

B.name: Black
B.philosophy: Black protects agency through cost, leverage, and refusal to remain powerless.

lore.summary: Black trusts self-determination over fairness and treats power as protection.
lore.narrative: Black does not wait for permission or rescue. It pays what must be paid and claims room to survive.

R.name: Red
R.philosophy: Red values freedom, honesty of feeling, and motion before paralysis.

lore.summary: Red trusts the living truth of the moment more than restraint or polish.
lore.narrative: Red would rather burn honestly than calcify politely. It moves because waiting changes the soul.

G.name: Green
G.philosophy: Green values harmony, instinct, and growth that respects the shape of life.

lore.summary: Green trusts the organism, the cycle, and the long memory of living systems.
lore.narrative: Green does not need to conquer time. It grows with it, and asks what the world already knows.

W.name: White
W.identity_blend: White expressed without a secondary color.

display.name: White
display.philosophy: White believes peace is not a mood. It is a structure: rules that hold, shelter that lasts, and obligations people can trust under pressure.
display.lore_summary: White does not seek order for its own sake. It builds order because order lets vulnerable people survive chaos, selfishness, and the failures of impulse.
display.core_tension: White protects through standards and systems, but its virtue can harden into over-control when safety becomes more important than listening.

drawn_to: Shared standards that protect the vulnerable
Fairness enforced through process
Structures that outlast individual moods
Group safety over private advantage
repelled_by: Treating every rule as oppression by default
Power that answers only to itself
Impulsive decisions that endanger others
Private exceptions that quietly become precedent
affinity.core_question: What structure keeps people safe when goodwill is not enough?
interview_tells: Frames care as duty, not only feeling
Talks about fairness in terms of standards and accountability
Wants clear expectations before conflict escalates
Sees systems as tools for shelter, not merely control
affinity.not_to_be_confused_with: Azorius trusts procedure above all; Boros acts faster in the face of harm; Selesnya anchors protection in belonging.

decree_voice.tone: Steady, protective, and exacting without cruelty.
decree_voice.speaks_like: A guardian who believes consistency is a form of mercy.
decree_voice.example_opening: The reading turns toward shelter, standards, and the work of making safety real.
decree_voice.example_decree: The reading turns toward shelter, standards, and the work of making safety real. White does not ask you to flatten every difference. It asks whether the structure holds when generosity fails. You protect by building something people can rely on, then standing beside it when the strain arrives.

deck_links.name: White Commanders
deck_links.desc: Tokens, taxes, equipment, and protective control lines for mono-white Commander starts.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Turns shared protection and ordered growth into a clean mono-white board plan.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: You want the deck to center taxes or equipment instead of a creature board.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Grows your angel board quickly and rewards a steady curve of protective, airborne threats.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Makes White's belief in collective pressure visible immediately through bodies and combat.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: You want a slower rules-and-taxes shell instead of a combat-focused table plan.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Creates attackers every combat and turns wide-board pressure into fast, disciplined damage.

native_fit_commanders.why_this_fits: Channels White's disciplined protection into a single armored line that ends games cleanly.
native_fit_commanders.skip_if: You prefer broad board control to a focused equipment threat.
native_fit_commanders.gameplay_summary: Loads equipment onto one resilient attacker and punishes opponents who cannot answer it on time.

weird_stretch_commanders.why_this_fits: Pushes White's protective instincts into a fiddlier rules-control shell where safety is created one layer at a time.
weird_stretch_commanders.skip_if: You want your White deck to end games quickly instead of grinding through timing tricks.
weird_stretch_commanders.gameplay_summary: Protects your board and disrupts interaction by turning color and protection into a constant rules puzzle.

advanced_complexity_commanders.gameplay_summary: Doubles your enters-the-battlefield value while constraining opposing triggers, letting patient sequencing become inevitability.

archetype_lanes.description: Go wide, protect the board, and turn collective structure into combat pressure.

discriminator_questions.question: What matters most when goodwill fails and people still need to be safe?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Separates White's shelter-and-standards logic from more private or expressive forms of care.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: The answer prioritizes reliable structure, shelter, or duty that protects more than one person at once.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: The answer rejects structure altogether or treats shared standards as inherently corrupt.

discriminator_questions.question: When protection and freedom pull apart, what must hold first?
discriminator_questions.purpose: Separates White from Red-aligned urgency and Blue-aligned procedural distance.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_supports_this_factio: The answer accepts limits, duties, or standards as the price of protecting the vulnerable.
discriminator_questions.answer_pattern_that_weakens_this_faction: The answer treats all limits as suspect regardless of who is left exposed.

collision_guidance.separator: White builds shelter and standards; Azorius further prioritizes procedure, precedent, and legitimacy.
collision_guidance.ask: If the system protects people but the paperwork is clumsy, do you repair the shelter or refine the procedure first?

collision_guidance.separator: White wants durable protection; Boros is faster to act when harm is already happening.
collision_guidance.ask: Is the first responsibility to build a structure that lasts, or to intervene before the next blow lands?

WU.identity_blend: White structure sharpened by Blue procedure.

UB.identity_blend: Blue patience weaponized by Black leverage.

BR.identity_blend: Black appetite turned public through Red spectacle.

RG.identity_blend: Red force returned to Green instinct and wild refusal.

WG.identity_blend: White protection rooted in Green belonging and communal growth.

WB.identity_blend: White structure hardened into Black obligation and collected debt.

UR.identity_blend: Blue curiosity accelerated by Red experimentation.

BG.identity_blend: Black survival stabilized by Green cycles of decay and renewal.

UG.identity_blend: Blue improvement grown through Green adaptation.

WR.identity_blend: White duty carried into action by Red conviction.

LOREHOLD.core_tension: Does history belong to order or to chaos? To careful systematic analysis or dangerous fieldwork? The college needs both traditions. Every student must choose - and then watch the choice shape everything afterward.
LOREHOLD.identity_blend: White duty and Red action turned toward memory, history, and excavation.

PRISMARI.core_tension: Does mastery of the medium precede authentic expression, or does authentic expression make technique meaningful? Both traditions are right. The tension between them is where the actual art lives.
PRISMARI.identity_blend: Blue spellcraft widened into Red performance and spectacle.

QUANDRIX.core_tension: Does math exist in the world, or in the mind? Are equations forces of nature waiting to be discovered, or frameworks constructed by minds? The College's most honest answer is that Esix exists and they're not entirely sure why.
QUANDRIX.identity_blend: Blue abstraction rooted in Green growth and scale.

SILVERQUILL.core_tension: Is eloquence a tool of service or self-advancement? The Radiance tradition holds that language is most powerful when it uplifts. The Shadow tradition holds that language flows toward individual power and pretending otherwise is the most dishonest thing a Silverquill mage can do. Both are right. The tension is the curriculum.
SILVERQUILL.identity_blend: White standards articulated through Black pressure, rhetoric, and status.

WITHERBLOOM.core_tension: Is life sacred because it creates and nourishes, or productive precisely because it ends? Both Lisette and Valentin are right about different aspects of the same process. Witherbloom students learn to hold both simultaneously.
WITHERBLOOM.identity_blend: Black appetite and Green cycle studied through vitality, biology, and exchange.

U.name: Blue
U.identity_blend: Blue expressed without a secondary color.

display.name: Blue
display.tagline: Possibility opens when the pattern is understood.
display.philosophy: Blue believes no one is finished by default. Knowledge, practice, and precise systems let people and worlds become more than their starting shape.
display.lore_summary: Blue does not act from impulse. It studies the variables, preserves options, and reshapes the future once the hidden structure is clear.
display.core_tension: Blue protects possibility through understanding, but its virtue can harden into paralysis when perfect information matters more than timely action.

drawn_to: Information treated as the first resource
Systems that improve through study and iteration
Patience before commitment
Tools, education, and planning that expand possible futures
repelled_by: Acting before the shape of the problem is understood
Treating nature, fate, or first instincts as final
Discarding options for the relief of immediate motion
Using power without a model of what happens next
affinity.core_question: What becomes possible once the hidden pattern is understood?
interview_tells: Waits for information before committing
Talks about options, systems, models, or repeatable improvement
Frames control as preparation rather than domination
Sees education, tools, and practice as liberation from default limits
affinity.not_to_be_confused_with: Azorius turns understanding into formal procedure; Dimir hides information as leverage; Izzet accelerates discovery into volatile testing; Simic applies improvement to living adaptation.

decree_voice.tone: Precise, patient, curious, and cool without contempt.
decree_voice.speaks_like: A strategist who believes every outcome has a structure waiting to be learned.
decree_voice.example_opening: The reading turns toward knowledge, options, and the discipline of acting after understanding.
decree_voice.example_decree: The reading turns toward knowledge, options, and the discipline of acting after understanding. Blue does not ask you to freeze forever. It asks you to map the hidden variables, keep the future open, and move when the pattern can be shaped instead of merely endured.

B.name: Black
B.identity_blend: Black expressed without a secondary color.

display.name: Black
display.tagline: Power is protection when no one is coming to save you.
display.philosophy: Black believes the world offers no guaranteed fairness. It secures agency by treating life, death, loyalty, and resources as costs that can be paid for control.
display.lore_summary: Black does not confuse self-preservation with cruelty. It asks what must be paid, what can be converted, and what leverage keeps its fate from belonging to someone else.
display.core_tension: Black protects the self through power and leverage, but its clarity can harden into isolation when every bond becomes a liability.

drawn_to: Self-determination when the world offers no guarantees
Power gained by paying costs others avoid
Resources converted into durable leverage
Death, loss, and sacrifice turned back into advantage
repelled_by: Waiting for fairness to arrive on its own
Moral purity that leaves people powerless
Dependence disguised as virtue
Systems that demand sacrifice without returning agency
affinity.core_question: What are you willing to pay so your fate stays yours?
interview_tells: Frames survival as a personal responsibility
Talks about costs, leverage, and agency without apology
Treats loss as material that can still be converted
Distrusts fairness when it is not backed by power
affinity.not_to_be_confused_with: Dimir hides leverage behind knowledge; Rakdos spends restraint in public intensity; Golgari turns death into ecosystem and cycle; Orzhov makes power visible through debt and obligation.

decree_voice.tone: Clear-eyed, unsentimental, and empowering without glamorizing cruelty.
decree_voice.speaks_like: A survivor who knows every bargain has a price and every price can become leverage.
decree_voice.example_opening: The reading turns toward cost, agency, and the refusal to remain powerless.
decree_voice.example_decree: The reading turns toward cost, agency, and the refusal to remain powerless. Black does not ask whether the world is fair before it acts. It asks what can be paid, what can be reclaimed, and what power will keep your fate from being signed away by someone else.

display.name: Red
display.tagline: The honest spark moves before the cage closes.
display.philosophy: Red believes feeling is a form of truth. Freedom becomes real when the impulse is allowed to move now, before fear, permission, or overthinking can smother it.
display.lore_summary: Red does not need cruelty, theater, primal belonging, or technical performance to prove itself. It trusts the present moment, ignites the next action, and lets emotion reveal what matters.
display.core_tension: Red protects aliveness through immediacy and freedom, but its virtue can burn out when every delay feels like a cage.

G.name: Green
G.identity_blend: Green expressed without a secondary color.

display.name: Green
display.tagline: The seed remembers what it is becoming.
display.philosophy: Green believes the world is not an unsolved machine. It is a living order already holding each creature's place, and strength comes from accepting nature, rooting deeply, and letting time reveal what was always in the seed.
display.lore_summary: Green listens for the old pattern beneath the noise: land, instinct, kinship with living systems, patient growth, and the quiet confidence to become what the world has already made possible.
display.core_tension: Green protects flourishing through acceptance and interdependence, but its virtue can harden into stagnation when every necessary change is dismissed as unnatural.
